content.comment_body: Hello everyone. I am working on a project to measure tank levels and need to transmit data to a PC located 4 kilometers away, using a program compatible with [product_name]. 1) What methods are available for sending the signal from [product_name] over 4 kilometers in a mountainous area without mobile signal? 2) Can anyone recommend a water tank level sensor with a 4-20 mA output? Thank you.
Hi, You might find helpful information in the following FAQ about setting up a remote connection to [product_name] using an analog modem via the telephone network.

To cover a distance of 4 km, a radio link is needed, but keep in mind that the farther the distance, the lower the bandwidth with typical frequencies. For example, a 2.4 GHz connection typically reaches only 300m, while 869 MHz can reach 3,000m but may not have enough bandwidth for [product_name] or software like [product_name] Soft Comfort. Modbus connections might be an option. Depending on terrain, repeaters may be required, and line-of-sight and weather play a big role. If you only need to check a sensor value, wireless Modbus sensors could be more practical, though they can be costly – expect to spend around 3,000 euros. Specialists from Schildknecht have experience assisting with radio link selection. For tank sensors, consider what the tank is made of, the type of liquid, and the maximum fill height. For tanks that don't freeze, tachometers or pressure sensors are suitable; ultrasonic or radar sensors often struggle with condensation. Monitoring tanks that freeze is difficult – pressure sensors may get damaged by ice. From my experience, I often use sensors from brands like Peppler & Fuchs, E&H, IFM, or [company_name]. Kind regards, [user_name]

There are several ways to transmit data from [product_name] over such a distance. If mobile service is available at your location, you could use a mobile communication module or interface module for [product_name]. Some modules allow a connection to the built-in web server where you can access data remotely, provided you have a SIM card with a public IP address. The same hardware can also send SMS notifications. Alternatively, certain modules allow data to be forwarded to AWS cloud dashboards, eliminating the need for a public IP. SMS notifications for power status are also supported. If mobile coverage isn’t available, some Wi-Fi routers permit longer distance connections, though in Europe the range is limited to about 300 meters and in the USA sometimes extends miles. Radio modems have also been used for such distances, but you must comply with local regulations regarding radio transmissions. Power line modems, which use the electrical network, could be another solution, though their effective range may not reach 3,000 meters. Good luck.

Thanks for the suggestions. I was advised to use a UHF controller which can transmit up to 20 km and handle two analog and two digital signals. This is from a company based in Greece, and I’m considering it. Has anyone used a UHF controller for this purpose? If more details are needed, I can share them.

As mentioned before, connecting two [product_name] devices at 869 MHz was very difficult due to insufficient bandwidth, even at just 6 meters apart, not because of the distance itself. Using Modbus might help, but I haven't tested it. Remember, local regulations in Greece may place limits on what frequencies and transmission power you can use, so be sure to check before proceeding. Greeting, [user_name]

I am not planning a network with two [product_name] controllers. Near the tank, I plan to use a VHF transmitter at 169 MHz (without [product_name]) that receives a 4-20 mA signal from the sensor and sends it up to 20 km as a 0-10 V signal. On the other side, I will have [product_name] receive the 0-10 V signal to measure tank levels from 0 to 6 meters. Currently, I am searching for a water level sensor for a 0-6 meter range with a 4-20 mA output.

How should the heading 'Remote [product_name] with no internet' be interpreted? Maybe we are misunderstanding each other or there are translation issues. You have a transmitter with a current input (0-20mA) using a 169 MHz transmission frequency and a 20 km range, with a paired receiver that outputs voltage? Examples of sensors from IFM you could use: Level probe models PS3417, PS3617, PS4607.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are discussing different methods for reliably monitoring water tank levels from a remote location using [product_name] hardware by [company_name], in an area without internet or mobile coverage, and separated by 4 kilometers. Various wireless solutions, including radio links, UHF/VHF controllers, Wi-Fi, modems, and possibilities for using cloud services, are debated, with limitations being bandwidth, compliance with radio laws, and environmental factors like terrain and weather. Selecting the right analog sensor for the tank involves practical considerations like tank material, the type of liquid, and risk of freezing.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to achieve dependable long-range data transmission for water tank level monitoring and to identify a compatible sensor for their specific environmental and technical requirements.
